manifest.name: dsh-sticky-notes
manifest.description: Sticky-notes wall in the Harness sidebar: capture ideas anytime and keep them.

bundle.text:
# dsh-sticky-notes bundle layer.
#   Host half (index.js): owns the notes file and the small local HTTP API the
#     browser half reads and writes through.
#   Client half (client.js): the sidebar panellist icon and the sticky-note wall
#     main panel, declared by package.json's dsh.client section.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-sticky-notes
      name: dsh-sticky-notes

readme.text:
A sticky-note wall inside DSH: one icon in the left sidebar, one panel to capture
ideas anytime, and a file on disk so nothing is lost when the page reloads or the
Harness restarts.

The bundle is self-contained: no dependencies, no build step, no configuration
required. It targets a DSH build that ships the `sidebar.panellist` slot
(`engines.dsh: ^0.2.1-alpha.2`).

From a terminal:

```sh
dsh plugin add github:LoveStudyXin/dsh-sticky-notes
```

Or from the GUI: open DSH → **Plugins / 插件** → **Add / 添加**, and paste the same
address. To install from a local checkout instead (edits apply on reload):

```sh
dsh plugin add link:/absolute/path/dsh-sticky-notes
```

Keep the bundle enabled and **refresh the page once** (or restart DSH if the
plugin manager asks for a restart). A sticky-note icon appears in the left rail;
click it to open the wall.

The wall lives on disk; see **Storage** for the paths, backups and export. A
Chinese install guide ships as [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md).

- **Sidebar entry** — a panel icon in the left rail; clicking it opens the wall.
- **Quick capture** — type in the box at the top and press `↵` to add a note
  (`⇧↵` for a new line). `⌘/Ctrl + ↵` also adds.
- **Images in the input** — paste a screenshot (`⌘V`/`Ctrl+V`), drag an image
  anywhere onto the wall, or pick files with the attach button. A note can carry
  up to 6 PNG/JPG/GIF/WebP images (≤8 MB each), shows thumbnails on the paper, and
  opens a full-size preview when a thumbnail is clicked (`Esc` closes).
- **Six paper colors**, a slight paper tilt, and a masonry wall.
- **Edit in place** — click a note's text, change it, click away (or `⌘/Ctrl + ↵`)
  to save; `Esc` cancels.
- **Pin** a note to the top, **delete** it with a 6-second **undo** toast.
- **Search** filters the wall; the footer shows saving state.
- **本地备份 / export / import** — the wall is copied to disk before every
  overwrite (last 30 kept), restorable from the header, and exportable or
  importable as a JSON file.
- Texts follow the active DSH locale (Chinese/English).

The Host half also registers a model-facing tool, so a Session can put a note on
the wall without a browser — including a Session started by an IM bot (Feishu,
WeChat, …), where the human just says “把这张图存到便利贴里”.

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | note text; optional when images are given |
| `color` | `amber` (default), `rose`, `sky`, `mint`, `lilac`, `tangerine` |
| `pinned` | pin the note to the top (default `false`) |
| `imagePaths` | image file paths: absolute, or relative to the calling Session's working directory (max 6) |

It reads the bytes itself and enforces the same rules as the panel (PNG/JPG/GIF/
WebP, ≤8 MB each, at most 6 images per note), appends one note to the same
`notes.json`, takes the same pre-overwrite backup, and returns
`{ noteId, noteCount, images }`.

The model does **not** need to see the picture: an IM bot stages a received image
into the workspace and hands the model a path, so even a text-only model can save
a screenshot it never “saw”.

The tool is registered when the plugin loads, so a linked development install
needs the plugin row to reload (disable then enable, or restart DSH) before a
Session can call it.

An IM message still costs a model turn — even when it only says “save this to a
sticky note”. `scripts/patch-dsh-im-sticky.mjs` patches the installed
`@xmanrui/dsh-im` bundle so a message that starts with `/sticky` is answered
without a Session turn: it writes the text and any staged images straight into
the wall and replies with the note id.

```sh

node scripts/patch-dsh-im-sticky.mjs --check   # report only
node scripts/patch-dsh-im-sticky.mjs           # apply (keeps lib/index.js.dsh-sticky.orig)
node scripts/patch-dsh-im-sticky.mjs --revert  # restore the unpatched bundle
```

Then disable and re-enable the “IM机器人” plugin (or restart DSH) and send
`/sticky 测试测试小肥鱼` in Feishu, with an image attached if you want one saved
too. `/sticky` is not in the plugin’s command panel or `/help` — type it.

Notes:

- The patch edits a third-party plugin in place. **A dsh-im upgrade overwrites
  it** — re-run the script afterwards (it verifies its anchors and refuses to
  guess on an unknown bundle version).
- The patched path skips the bot’s command-permission check, so keep the bot’s
  allowlist tight.
- The wall is a single JSON file with last-write-wins writes: an open sticky
  panel that saves a stale wall can overwrite a note saved from IM. Reload the
  panel after an IM save if you keep it open.

Everything is local-first; the wall can additionally push each note to a Feishu
Bitable (多维表格) table. It is **one-way and additive**: local files remain the
source of truth, editing or deleting a note locally does not change its row, and
Feishu being unreachable never blocks a local save (failures are logged and
retried on the next tick).

Setup:

1. The Feishu app needs `bitable:app` (or `base:app:create`) and `drive:drive`.
   Open the authorization link the setup script prints, have an admin approve it
   and publish a version.
2. Run the setup script — it reuses the bot’s app credentials from DSH, creates
   “DSH 便利贴” with the fields `文字 / 颜色 / 置顶 / 创建时间 / 图片`, and writes
   `$DSH_HOME/state/sticky-notes/feishu.json`:

```sh
   node scripts/setup-feishu-bitable.mjs --check   # token + what is missing
   node scripts/setup-feishu-bitable.mjs           # create and configure
   ```

3. Reload the sticky-notes plugin (or restart DSH). New notes are mirrored
   within a second or two; the wall is also polled every 30 s as a fallback.

How it works:

- `feishu.json` (in the data dir) holds `enabled`, `appId`, `secretRef`,
  `appToken`, `tableId`, `baseUrl` and `backfillNotes`. Delete it or set
  `enabled: false` to stop mirroring.
- `feishu-sync.json` remembers which note ids were pushed, so a restart never
  duplicates rows. Pointing at a different Bitable resets that history.
- With `backfillNotes: true` (the setup default) the existing wall is pushed
  once; set it to `false` to start from the next new note only.
- Each image is uploaded as a Bitable attachment (`drive/v1/medias/upload_all`,
  `parent_type=bitable_image`); a failed image upload still pushes the row
  without that image.

Everything is a local file; nothing lives only in the browser.

Paths below are under `$DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`):

- `$DSH_HOME/state/sticky-notes/notes.json` — the wall itself.
- `$DSH_HOME/state/sticky-notes/images/<id>.<ext>` — pasted image bytes.
- `$DSH_HOME/state/sticky-notes/backups/notes-<timestamp>-<count>.json` — the wall
  **before an overwrite** (up to 30 kept; at most one per 30 s of editing). Images a
  backup still references are kept too, so a restored backup never shows broken
  pictures.

`config.dataDir` in `cordis.patch.yml` moves the whole directory. It is a plain
string (no schema, no `~` expansion): give an **absolute** path.

Limits: one wall holds at most 5000 notes and 64 MB of JSON per save; notes beyond
that are dropped on write. Two windows on the same wall use last-write-wins.

Three ways to get data back or copy it out:

1. **备份** in the panel header lists the local backups with their note count and
   restore time; one click restores that wall.
2. **导出** downloads the current wall as `sticky-notes-<date>.json`.
3. **导入** replaces the whole wall from a previously exported (or hand-edited)
   JSON file; entries that cannot be rendered are skipped, and the server backs up
   the current wall first.

The backup popover also shows the absolute `notes.json` path. Only requests from
the GUI itself (same-origin browser fetches) or from local tools are served;
uploads must carry the same-origin request marker, and image bytes — not the
declared content-type — decide the accepted formats.

A note references images by `{ id, type, size }`; the bytes are served at
`/sticky-notes/images/<id>.<ext>`, and bytes no note or backup references are
collected after a 10-minute grace period on the next save.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Host half: notes file, normalization, local HTTP API, `sticky_notes_add` tool |
| `feishu-sync.js` | Optional one-way mirror: new notes → Feishu 多维表格 |
| `scripts/setup-feishu-bitable.mjs` | Optional: create the Bitable table and write `feishu.json` |
| `scripts/patch-dsh-im-sticky.mjs` | Optional: patch dsh-im so an IM `/sticky` message skips the model |
| `client.js` | Client half: sidebar panellist icon + `main` panel |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch inserting the plugin row |
| `locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json` | Display title/description for the plugin manager |
| `icon.svg` | Original icon |
